[WP] You've found out humans hold within them a wonderful secret...

The sky above was white gray, waiting to rain on us but not ready to quite yet. There were hundreds of people at the train station. Just a year ago that would mean huge commotion, loud noises - children laughing, the elder talking slowly among the crowd, young lovers hugging and maybe a local band giving off a performance in exchange for some coins. Today though it was eerily silent, no one had even the inclination to complain or cry. Everything had changed since the Blight.

A few months ago this disease had appeared from out of nowhere. By the time scientists, doctors and the media figured out what was happening, society as we knew was already gone, at least partway. It was such a fast and lethal virus that in mere weeks we started noticing that radios and TV stations no longer had the personnel to be on-air 24/7; hospitals quickly grew understaffed - not only because their doctors and nurses started to succumb to it but also due to infected masses flocking in looking for help; small restaurants and stores were closing on a daily basis. Not long after, there weren't enough people to man the supply lines and shortage of food and all products became the norm worldwide. The bigger cities, that didn't produce their own sustenance thinned out almost immediately and other cities vanished as well, not being able to support themselves anymore without outside help.

I used to live in the east coast. What little family I had left were gone in months after the Blight had started. In a way, I'm happy they weren't alive to suffer from the aftermath. I used to live in Philadelphia but when we couldn't find food on the markets anymore I had to go. We gathered a group of friends and left. Slowly we went from town to town all the way to the west coast, hearing rumors that Russia was sending help to us there. It wasn't true though, or it if was, we never found it. Of the friends I've left with, some fell to the disease as well and others left the group to try their luck elsewhere. When the few of us remaining started discussing whether we should start attacking other folk for food and money then I knew it was my own time to leave. I hugged them and said goodbye, knowing I'd never see them again, for better or worse.

And so here is where I am. I traveled south to Mexico after walking, hitching and riding through most of the US since I left home. The virus seems to have slowed by now - maybe those who are left are the ones immune to it - but I'd wager the face of the world... or rather, society's is now changed forever, beyond the point of no return.

The crowded train station is eerily silent, people flocking beneath whatever roof they can find even though the rain hasn't started yet. I look at people's faces and I know how they feel, because I feel the same - they've left home, they've lost friends and family, they went through hardships and none could see a rainbow at the end of the long road. While I gazed through their faces my eyes met a young woman, her clothes dirty and her hair uncared for. She looked as if she carried the weight of the world in her shoulders. She noticed me looking at her.

She looked back at me, all by herself. For an instant she seemed startled, then suspicious. Then her eyes seemed to tear up a little as if she was about to cry for help. And then the most wonderful thing happened: in the midst of all the misery, she smiled back at me. An open, broad smile that made her eyes close a little. She was beautiful and watching her I knew that everything would be alright, eventually...

Half-unaware I was doing it, I moved over to her side, wondering what secret would make her hold on to hope while her world's falling apart.
